Headteacher's Welcome
A warm welcome to Earlham Primary School, where learning extends far beyond the classroom.
We are a nurturing and inclusive school where children thrive in a happy, safe and well-resourced environment. Earlham is a hidden gem at the heart of our community, cherished by families for its nurturing ethos, ambitious curriculum and exceptional opportunities.
As a popular and growing school, we continue to maintain the warmth, sense of belonging and strong family partnerships that make Earlham such a special place to learn.
Ambition and high expectations underpin everything we do, inspiring every child to aim high, work hard and believe in their potential. We are committed to ensuring that all pupils receive the challenge, encouragement and support they need to flourish, celebrate their achievements and reach their full potential.
Set within extensive grounds, Earlham provides a rich outdoor environment that enhances both learning and wellbeing. Pupils enjoy access to spacious playgrounds, a Multi-Use Games Area (MUGA), gardens and dedicated environmental spaces that encourage exploration, creativity and physical activity.
At Earlham, our dedicated team of staff, including specialist teachers, is passionate about delivering an education that inspires curiosity, builds confidence and enables every pupil to achieve excellence. We believe that children learn best when they feel valued, supported and excited by their learning.
We are proud to offer a wide range of enrichment opportunities designed to broaden horizons and foster a lifelong love of learning. Through sports, music, art, drama and language activities, as well as educational visits, special events and outdoor experiences, pupils are encouraged to explore their interests, discover new passions and develop their individual talents.
This year, we are especially proud to be working in partnership with Wigmore Hall, the world-renowned centre for chamber music and music education. This exciting collaboration provides our pupils with exceptional opportunities to experience live performances, develop their musical understanding and be inspired by world-class artists.
Our school is beautifully situated in N22, close to Alexandra Palace and surrounded by wide green open spaces. This unique location provides a calm and inspiring setting for children to learn and play, while also offering access to a wealth of cultural opportunities.
In recent years, Earlham has been transformed through the opening of our modern school building in 2020 and the development of expansive outdoor learning spaces in 2021. Our pupils now benefit from excellent facilities, including dedicated rooms for art and design, reading, cookery, music and performance, alongside our beautifully landscaped playground and MUGA.
We are particularly fortunate to have a dedicated Forest School, where children learn through hands-on experiences that nurture resilience, teamwork, independence and problem-solving skills. These opportunities help pupils develop a strong connection with the natural world while building confidence and curiosity.
To further support our families, we offer high-quality wraparound care before and after school. This provision provides a safe, engaging and nurturing environment, with enjoyable activities, healthy snacks and opportunities for social interaction, giving parents flexibility and reassurance throughout the school day.
We are proud of the strong partnerships we have built with families, local organisations, cultural institutions and the wider community. Together, we create a supportive network that enriches learning and helps every child thrive.
Children have only one childhood, and we believe their primary school years should be filled with wonder, inspiration and memorable experiences that foster a lifelong love of learning.
If you would like to visit our school and experience the warmth, energy and sense of community that make Earlham so special, we would be delighted to welcome you.

Our School Values
At Earlham, everything we do is guided by a set of shared values that help every child feel safe, included, inspired and ready to achieve their very best. These values shape our learning, our relationships and our school community every day.
Small acts of kindness make a big difference.We choose empathy, understanding and encouragement every day.
We show respect by caring for ourselves, each other and our environment.Every voice is valued, and everyone is treated with kindness and fairness.
We take responsibility for our learning, our behaviour and our choices.We work hard, stay curious and always try our best.
We keep going, even when things are difficult.We encourage children to develop resilience, try new challenges and never give up.
We embrace diversity and value each other’s differences.We listen, learn and show acceptance towards all cultures, backgrounds and beliefs
What these values look like in everyday school life
We are committed to making our school a place where every child feels safe, happy and ready to learn. Our values guide us in building a community where everyone can thrive.
Warm, positive relationships between children and adults
Celebrations of diversity, culture and individuality
British Values
At Earlham, British Values are not taught in isolation—they are woven through our daily practice, our curriculum and our school values. Here is how each British Value connects naturally to the values we promote every day.
Linked School Values: Respectful · Kind · Responsible
In practice: School council, class voting, pupil leadership, shared decision‑making.
In our school, children share their views and ideas through our elected School Council, which follows a child‑friendly democratic voting process. The council meets regularly to discuss school priorities and contributes to staff recruitment by meeting candidates and offering feedback.
Subject leaders also gather pupil voice through conferencing and surveys, helping us evaluate the curriculum and improve key areas such as behaviour and wellbeing.
Linked School Values: Responsible · Respectful · Perseverance
In practice: Clear expectations, behaviour systems, restorative approaches, learning about laws in society.
We teach our children why rules and laws exist, how they protect us, and the consequences when they are not followed. Through RSHE and assemblies, the themes of trust, honesty and respect are explored helping them to develop a strong sense of right and wrong.
Our trauma‑informed behaviour policy ensures pupils understand expectations, rewards and consequences. We also work closely with local police officers and other important professionals, who visit to explain their role in the community. As part of our TfL Stars work, the children help promote traffic safety outside the school, supporting a safe environment at the start and end of the day.
Linked School Values: Responsible · Kind · Perseverance
In practice: Choice in learning, celebrating uniqueness, safe risk‑taking, encouraging independence.
At our school, children are encouraged to make positive choices, try new things and take responsibility for their learning. We support them to develop confidence, independence and high aspirations.
We support every child recognise their strengths, express their ideas and understand that they have the freedom to be themselves within a safe and supportive environment.
The children are taught how to keep themselves safe—both in and out of school. This includes understanding personal boundaries, consent. Through our RSHE curriculum and the NSPCC PANTS lessons, the children are taught that their body belongs to them.
Linked School Values: Respectful · Kind · Perseverance
In practice: Teamwork, positive relationships, anti‑bullying work, celebrating achievements.
Are children are taught that mutual respect means valuing each other’s ideas, feelings and differences. It involves treating others how we would like to be treated and understanding that everyone deserves kindness and fairness. This is central to building a positive, inclusive school community where children feel safe, valued and able to learn.
Our staff consistently model good manners, active listening, turn‑taking and positive language throughout the school day to teach children what respectful behaviour looks and sounds like.
Across the school behaviour expectations and school values are reinforced to help children understand what respect means in everyday situations—sharing, cooperating, and resolving disagreements calmly. In addition, each class creates and signs a class contract at the start of each academic year.
Through our RSHE and PSHE lessons, children are taught about friendships, feelings, fairness and understanding others. These lessons help them develop empathy and respect for different backgrounds, abilities and beliefs.
Tolerance of Those with Different Faiths and Beliefs
Linked School Values: Tolerant · Kind · Respectful
In practice: RE lessons, cultural celebrations, assemblies, visitors, community links.
Pupils are Earlham learn that difference is something to be welcomed and celebrated. We promote and celebrate diversity through a range of activities including assemblies, whole school events and stories. We also ensure that our curriculum links help pupils appreciate different cultures, faiths and perspectives.
Group activities, partner work and class discussions help children learn to listen, take turns, appreciate other viewpoints and work towards shared goals.
When disagreements occur, children are guided to reflect, listen to each other and repair relationships. This builds understanding, empathy and responsibility for their actions.

Determined that our pupils leave Earlham as confident, responsible, life-long learners who are able to make a positive contribution to society, we strive to create a learning community, rich in opportunity, where everyone is valued, empowered and challenged to achieve their potential and excel in their achievements.
Through our caring and inclusive learning environment, we aim to nurture and develop mutual respect, tolerance and teamwork - encouraging pupils to embrace diversity and value one another equally.

Welcome
Welcome to our school and school website.
We are an ambitious, inclusive and vibrant primary community where every child is encouraged to aim high, work hard and believe in their potential.
We set high expectations for all our pupils and work tirelessly to provide the challenge, encouragement and support they need to flourish, celebrate their accomplishments and reach their full potential.
At Earlham, our dedicated team of staff, which includes specialist teachers, is deeply committed to providing an education that inspires curiosity, nurtures confidence and supports every pupil to achieve excellence.
We are proud to offer a rich programme of enrichment opportunities that broaden children’s horizons and deepen their love for learning. From sports, arts and STEM clubs to events, visits and outdoor learning, Earlham pupils can explore their passions, discover new interests and develop their unique talents.
This year we feel especially proud to be working in partnership with the prestigious Wigmore Hall, a world‑renowned centre for chamber music and music education.
Our school is beautifully nestled between wide green open spaces, creating a calm and inspiring setting for children to learn and play. Located in N22, just a short distance from Alexandra Palace, we benefit from a unique blend of natural surroundings and rich cultural opportunities.
In recent years, our school has been transformed through the opening of our modern building (in 2020) and the creation of expansive outdoor learning spaces (in 2021). Our pupils now benefit from excellent facilities, including dedicated rooms for art and design, reading, cookery, music and performance, as well as a multi‑use games area (MUGA) within our beautifully landscaped playground.
We are incredibly fortunate to have a spacious outdoor environment that promotes exploration, curiosity and wellbeing, including a dedicated Forest School where children learn through hands‑on activities that build resilience, teamwork and problem‑solving.
To support our families, we provide high‑quality wraparound care before and after school. Our provision offers a safe, engaging and nurturing environment with enjoyable activities, healthy snacks and opportunities for social interaction, giving parents flexibility and reassurance throughout the school day.
We are proud of the strong partnerships we have developed with families, local organisations, cultural institutions and the wider community. Together, we create a supportive network that enhances learning and ensures every child thrives.
Children have only one childhood, and we believe their primary school years should be filled with wonder, inspiration and memorable learning experiences.
If you would like to visit and experience the warmth, energy and sense of community that make Earlham so special, we would be delighted to meet you.

Breakfast Club
At Earlham Primary School we are committed to supporting our families by offering high-quality wraparound childcare. Our wraparound provision ensures that all our children have access to safe, inclusive, and engaging childcare from 8am to 6.00pm during term time. This is designed to meet the needs of working parents and provide a seamless extension of the school day.
We offer families a variety of options to extend the school day to suit our families needs.
Breakfast club
Our 'before school care' breakfast club operates from 8am until 8.45am.
Our Breakfast club ensures great provision for children from Reception through to Year 6. Children enjoy a healthy breakfast and an active start to the day with their friends in our school dining hall. They are looked after by staff from school who provide quiet games and activities until the school day begins in the main school building.
Please contact the school office for further information
£10 per full session (straight after school until 6pm)
We ask that payments are made using ScoPay.

Music
At our school, we aim to inspire a love of music and develop pupils’ confidence, creativity, and appreciation of a wide range of musical styles.
Music is an integral part of school life at Earlham and is key to offering our children a broad and varied curriculum of study from our pupils in our Early Years provision to Year 6; it develops a range of important skills within our children such as listening and evaluation skills as well as developing fine and gross motor control.
We are passionate about music and committed to ensuring that our children have the best opportunities possible to develop their musical knowledge and skills alongside self-confidence, attentive curiosity and creativity.
Our music curriculum is structured using the Charanga scheme of work, which provides a progressive and inclusive approach to music education from Early Years through to Key Stage 2.
Charanga supports pupils in developing the key musical skills of listening, appraising, composing, improvising, and performing. Lessons are carefully sequenced to build knowledge and skills over time, allowing children to deepen their understanding of musical elements such as rhythm, pitch, tempo, and dynamics. Pupils are introduced to a diverse range of musical genres and traditions, helping them to develop a broad and balanced musical appreciation.
Practical music-making is at the heart of our curriculum. Throughout their musical journey, pupils have regular opportunities to sing, play instruments, and perform. Children learn to play the glockenspiel as part of their classroom learning, developing their ability to read notation and perform with increasing accuracy and expression.
We aim to develop pupils who are confident performers and enthusiastic listeners, with a lifelong appreciation of music through collaboration and creativity.
In Year 4, all pupils have the opportunity to learn the violin as part of a whole-class instrumental programme. This experience enables children to develop discipline, resilience, and a sense of achievement as they learn a new and challenging instrument. Termly violin concerts provide pupils with the opportunity to perform to an audience, building confidence and celebrating their progress.
Pupils who develop a passion for the violin are encouraged to continue their learning beyond Year 4, with opportunities to build on their skills through to Year 6. This ensures continuity and allows pupils to further develop their musical ability over time.
This year we are proud to be working in partnership with the prestigious Wigmore Hall. The fantastic programme on offer both enriches and inspires our curriculum offer by exposing our pupils to musical excellence and encouraging them to further develop a love and appreciation of music and musical performance.
We believe that music is a universal language that can be spoken by all members of our diverse and inclusive school community. We are passionate about exploring ways to enrich our music provision and providing our pupils with meaningful opportunities to explore, create and enjoy music.
We strongly believe that a high-quality music education is vital for all pupils and working collaboratively with Haringey’s excellent Music Education Hub and Wigmore Hall both strengthens the ties between the school and the wider school community and contributes to the happiness and wellbeing of our children and staff.
" I have been visiting Earlham Primary on a weekly basis as a peripatetic music teacher for over a decade. The school is a calm and bright environment. Kindness is key at this school. The children are at the heart of every decision made. Their headteacher is an inspiring leader who has built a team of teachers who I never hear shouting; I see care and patience in their interactions with the children. It is a pleasure to work with the school staff and the students at this school."

This is a summary of how our school delivers music education to all our pupils across three areas – curriculum music, co-curricular provision and musical experiences – and what changes we are planning in future years. This information is to help pupils and parents or carers understand what our school offers and who we work with to support our pupils’ music education.
Part A: Curriculum music
This is about what we teach in lesson time, how much time is spent teaching music and any music qualifications or awards that pupils can achieve.
At Earlham children have a rich musical curriculum starting from our two-year old provision all the way to Year 6.
In the Early Years music is embedded in the everyday provision; children sing songs related to routines, hear music from other cultures, clap rhythms, learn rhymes, and use percussion instruments. From Year 1 upwards, music is timetabled for all year groups. We use an adapted version of the Charanga scheme modified to account for our whole school projects. Children listen, perform and compose, and building on their skills and vocabulary in a careful sequence, including simple notation.
Children are taught to play Glockenspiels and Violins, as well as a variety of percussion instruments, and learn to use their own bodies and voices rhythmically and musically. Children at Earlham are exposed to music from a variety of cultures and genres.
Part B: Extra-curricular music
Earlham Primary school is proud to be in a three-year partnership with Wigmore Hall/. We also work closely with the Haringey Music Hub. Children can continue learning the violin in Year 5, attend musical after school clubs, such as Musical Theatre and Musical Elements run by outside providers. Children also have weekly singing assemblies which are led by qualified specialist music teacher.
Part C: Musical events
This is about all the other musical events and opportunities that we organise, concerts and shows, and trips to professional concerts.
Pupils at Earlham take part in many different musical events, both as attendees and as performers. Each year the Early Years and Key Stage 1 perform festive shows for parents/carers, Year 4 put on violin performances, individual classes perform in their assemblies, and Year 6 host an annual talent show featuring a variety of songs and instruments. Children visit concert halls and festivals to watch professional artists, and visiting musicians play to children in assemblies.
In the future
This is about what the school is planning for subsequent years.
We are excited to be develop plans to build on our partnership with Wigmore Hall to further enhance our music provision in a number of ways which include offering individual music lessons, putting together a school ensemble, and committing to continuous professional development relating to music. We are also focusing on improving access to our children with SEND.

Art
Art at Earlham focuses on celebrating individuality and diversity through creative representation. We recognise that each child has a different story and we aim to represent this by exploring a range of cultures to deliver the art curriculum. We believe that every child is an artist and it is up to us to provide them with high quality teaching to make room for a natural appreciation for fine arts.
Art sessions will have close curricular links to each current topic to provide all children opportunities to express their knowledge of particular subjects. We will encourage the use of key vocabulary, skills and techniques and provide our pupils with rich language relating to different artist/styles of work.
We have high expectations of pupils and encourage them to appreciate that art cannot be rushed. To capture high quality work, art lessons may take the form of project based work to provide sufficient time to complete each piece. This may be spread over several weeks. We ensure that we are supporting children to progress their artistic knowledge and skills by providing them with opportunities to practice the skills and techniques they have learnt.
EYFS: Opportunities for art will be available daily either indoors or outside. This does not have to be as an adult led activity. Monitoring and recording will be via Tapestry, in Special Books or available to view on displays.
KS1/2: Each child will have an individual art book. This will be an ongoing book through the child’s journey at Earlham to clearly model the progression throughout the years. Art will be regularly monitored with the use of whole class sketch books. The art/scrap book is used to document key pieces and projects over the course of the academic year. It will be used for monitoring purposes, marking and feedback. Art sessions will alternate half termly with DT.
All children across the school will be expected to be exposed to key vocabulary relating to their focus skill/artist/technique.
Our children and staff benefit from working closely with a specialist art teachers who works with us on a weekly basis.
We understand that art can be therapeutic and encourage a calm and tranquil environment during art sessions. We are committed to supporting children to feel safe and free to self-express during these sessions.
There will be annual art events/projects involving the whole school. Children will be expected to participate and produce work of a high standard. These projects will be used to bring the school community together and also involve parents and carers.

Computing
The National Curriculum Purpose of Study states that:
A high-quality computing education equips pupils to use computational thinking and creativity to understand and change the world. Computing has deep links with mathematics, science and design and technology, and provides insights into both natural and artificial systems. The core of computing is computer science, in which pupils are taught the principles of information and computation, how digital systems work and how to put this knowledge to use through programming. Building on this knowledge and understanding, pupils are equipped to use information technology to create programs, systems and a range of content. Computing also ensures that pupils become digitally literate – able to use, and express themselves and develop their ideas through, information and communication technology – at a level suitable for the future workplace and as active participants in a digital world.
Whilst the Computing Curriculum has an increased focus on Computer Science including developing pupils’ programming skills and their understanding of what happens ‘behind the scenes’, it is important that they also continue to develop their Digital Literacy and e-safety capability and our school curriculum us designed to reflect this.
Computers are part of nearly every aspect of modern life. Through teaching computing, we intend to equip children to participate in a rapidly-changing world where work and leisure activities are increasingly transformed and enhanced by technology. Computing skills and knowledge are a major factor in enabling children to be confident, creative and independent learners, which is what we want for all pupils at Earlham Primary School. We intend to give our pupils the knowledge and understanding that will be essential for a future which is going to be heavily reliant on computers and technology along with the necessary skills and experience to access the opportunities and challenges that they will encounter. This includes enabling them to be independent critical thinkers who can use their knowledge and understanding to problem solve. At Earlham Primary, we believe it essential that children learn how to use a wide range of technologies and are exposed to a variety of software to build their knowledge and confidence in computing. It is our intention to ensure that all our pupils receive this exposure and become familiar with many areas of computing through the teaching of our curriculum.
At Earlham Primary School, teachers are encouraged to progressively develop pupils’ Computing skills and capability through discrete learning opportunities, and also to exploit this capability as a tool to support objectives in other curriculum areas meaningfully. These links include, but are not limited to, the use of a range digital devices in a wide range of contexts. Opportunities are provided for children to learn using technology as well as about the theory behind computing. These opportunities may well be presented within other subject areas (e.g. sequencing instructions in English, problems solving in Maths or isolating variables in Science). In this way Computing and the use of technology become integrated into the curriculum and are used as a truly beneficial tool for learning.
At Key Stages 1 and 2, the planning, organisation and delivery of the Computing curriculum is supported by National Centre for Computing Education (NCCE) https://teachcomputing.org/. Some units are also delivered using Barefoot Computing or Switched On (see Computing Curriculum Overview).
In the EYFS, opportunities for the use of technology are an integral part of each area of learning and the school ensures that children have opportunities to engage in Computational Thinking (see appendix 1).
Assessment for learning will take place during lessons and at the end of modules to ensure that misconceptions are addressed and so that the children make good progress in their computing lessons
Computing also covers online safety (see Online Safety Policy for details) which is taught to the pupils regularly through Project Evolve to ensure they know how to use digital technology safely and responsibly at school and at home. Project Evolve cover all eight aspects of online safety: Self-image and Identity, Online Relationships, Online Reputation, Online Bullying, Managing Online Information, Privacy and Security, Copyright and Ownership and Health, Well-being and Lifestyle. More details about online safety at Earlham Primary can be found in our online safety policy.
Teaching and Learning Approaches
When delivering the National Curriculum for Computing, teachers are expected to employ a range of strategies and to use their professional judgement to decide on the most appropriate teaching and learning approach for the class, groups of pupils or individual pupils.
Approaches and strategies used may include:
Access and Inclusion
Each pupil’s access to technology varies greatly dependent on the nature of the activity they are involved in (e.g. some activities benefit from prolonged access to a computer whilst other are best served with brief access to a digital device for a focussed purpose). However, on average, pupils have approximately 6 hours allocated to Computing each half term using a mixture of unplugged activities and the following technology:
In addition to discrete Computing sessions, opportunities to develop and extend Computing capability are provided in other curriculum areas and technology is used to support most other subject areas. All children have equality of access to appropriate technology in order to develop their personal Computing capability. When children are working in groups, we endeavour to ensure that their hands-on experience is equitable. We check resources, software and documentation to ensure that gender and ethnicity are reflected in a balanced way without stereotyping.
Children with access to technology at home are encouraged to use it for educational benefit and online safety guidance is offered to both pupils and parents where appropriate.
Extended Opportunities for Learning
The school uses a variety of online tools and environments to extend learning opportunities beyond the classroom. Our online learning tools allow pupils to access learning materials and tools anytime, anywhere and provide channels of communication to both adults and children alike and break down barriers to learning. Our online learning tools are also used to teach children the skills and capabilities they need to stay safe and well in the digital world. Other examples of Extended Opportunities for Learning at Earlham Primary School include:
The Computing Subject Leader follows a systematic and regular programme of evaluation and monitoring of the Computing curriculum, across the school. This is so that she / he can monitor the quality of education being provided to all pupils, including: • Checking that the school’s curriculum ‘Implementation’ matches its ‘Intent’
As a result of monitoring, appropriate CPD opportunities are provided for staff on an individual, group and whole school basis in line with the school’s School Development Plan. A record of these opportunities is kept by the Subject Leader.
Recording and Assessment
Pupils’ work is recorded in individual Computing folders. Teachers use assessment for learning to gauge those who have met the overall objectives across the unit and those that require further support.
At the end of a unit, teachers gather a random sample of pupil voice that highlights the learning and use the assessment slide at the end of lesson to gather children’s self-assessment.
Where children are identified as requiring additional support, teachers adapt lessons so that pupils are supported by their peers or the adult in the class.
Pupils’ achievement and attainment is measured against the relevant National Curriculum requirements at the end of each Key Stage and reported according to government guidelines (including statutory requirements for reporting to parents).
The impact of our curriculum is that throughout their time at Earlham Primary, our pupils will demonstrate progression in their computing skills and complete a variety of tasks and projects related to the computing curriculum.
Children will build on skills learnt in previous year groups and leave Earlham Primary with a broad understanding of computing and the ability to use their computing skills to help them solve problems and achieve outcomes. These skills will also translate into other areas of the curriculum including mathematics, science, design technology and art.
Finally, our pupils will leave with a solid understanding of online safety, the risks which they may face and how to deal with these risks (see our online safety policy for more detail).

DT
Intent
DT at Earlham focuses on celebrating individuality and diversity through creative representation. We recognise that each child has a different story and we aim to represent this by exploring a range of cultures to deliver the DT curriculum. We believe that every child is capable of extraordinary designs and we aim to provide them with high quality teaching to create the best possible outcomes.
DT sessions will have close curricular links to each current topic to provide all children opportunities to express their knowledge on particular subjects. We will encourage the use of key vocabulary of skills and techniques and provide children with rich language relating to their artist/style of work.
We have high expectations from all our children and we encourage and understand that DT cannot be rushed. To capture high quality work, DT sessions may take the form of project based work to provide sufficient time to complete each piece. This may be spread over several weeks. We will ensure that we are supporting children to progress in their DT knowledge and skill base by building up on skills and techniques and providing opportunities to practice. We aim to ensure children will have access to appropriate tools and develop the accurate and most effective skills to use them.
Overview and implementation
EYFS: Opportunities for DT will be available daily either indoors or outside. This does not have to be as an adult led activity. Monitoring and recording will be via Tapestry, in Special Books or available to view on displays. Using a range of malleable materials daily/weekly with interventions of skill progression and use of appropriate tools. Weekly cooking activities will take place with a group of focus children. Junk modelling will be available for children to access throughout the day.
KS1/2: Each child will have an individual scrap book. This will be an ongoing book through the child’s journey at Earlham to clearly model the progression throughout the years. DT will be regularly monitored with the use of whole class sketch books. The art/scrap book is used to document key pieces and projects over the course of the academic year. It will be used for monitoring purposes, marking and feedback. DT sessions will alternate half termly with art. Cooking opportunities will happen at least once a term.
All children across the school will be expected to be exposed to key vocabulary relating to their focus skill/artist/technique.
We understand that DT can be therapeutic and we encourage a calm and tranquil environment during DT sessions. We are dedicated to supporting children to feel safe and free to self-express during these sessions.
There will be annual art events/projects involving the whole school. Children will be expected to participate and produce work of a high standard. These projects will be used to bring the school community together and also involve parents and carers.

Reading
At Earlham, our aim is for all children to learn to read fluently and with confidence, regardless of their background, needs or ability. We strive to foster a love of reading at school and at home and believe reading is an entitlement that should enable children to connect with the wider world and provide them with a fundamental life skill. Therefore, reading is at the very heart of our curriculum. We are committed to promoting a love for reading and not only giving children opportunities to read in English and Reading lessons, but in the wider curriculum too.
The curriculum is delivered through Little Wandle phonics, (a systematic and synthetic phonics programme), a linked approach to shared and guided reading using the Destination Reader pedagogy, regular opportunities for independent reading and hearing quality texts read aloud every day. We start teaching phonics in Nursery/Reception which ensures pupils build on their growing knowledge of the alphabetic code, mastering phonics to read and spell as they move through the school.
We make use of high-quality texts in both reading lessons and across the curriculum to provide challenging reading opportunities outside of the reading lessons. To enable all our pupils to see themselves in the books they read, we ensure our books in school reflect the diversity of our community and the wider world. All of these are essential components needed to develop fluent, enthusiastic and critical readers.
It is important that children are motivated to read at home regularly; when their reading opportunities increase, so does their fluency and stamina which in turn increases their enjoyment of reading. Therefore, the link between children’s motivation to read and reading for pleasure is reciprocal. Furthermore, we know that reading for pleasure is beneficial not only for reading outcomes, but for wider learning enjoyment and mental wellbeing. We understand the significance of parents and carers in supporting their children to develop both word reading and comprehension skills so we endeavour to build a home-school partnership which enables parents and carers to have the confidence to support their children with reading at home.

KS2 Whole Class Reading – Destination Reader
Why we use Destination Reader
‘Destination Reader’, as a pedagogy, has been embedded in all KS2 classes with consistency between all year groups. Children read aloud to each other and to the teacher which supports them to understand the meaning of new words they meet as well as correct themselves and each other when they are reading.
Modelling of text discussion is an important feature of the pedagogy. Children work in pairs to discuss the text through applying the strategies from the National Curriculum. This provides children with the opportunity to agree, challenge and build on each others’ ideas using systematic use of a series of language stems.
Discussion of texts is a key focus for Earlham and is embedded and replicated in other curricular areas like Geography and History reading where reading material is emulated. Importance is placed on listening to and discussing a wide range of fiction, poetry, non-fiction and reading books that are structured in different ways and reading for a range of purposes, including diversity and those featuring other minority areas such as disability.
In KS2, DR lessons will focus on either a different fiction, non-fiction or poetry text every half-term.

Reading for Pleasure
We highly value reading for pleasure and work hard as a school to grow our Reading for Pleasure pedagogy. We read to children every day to promote the love of reading. We choose these books carefully as we want children to experience a wide range of books, including books that reflect the children at Earlham as well as books that open windows into other worlds and cultures. Every classroom has access to a range of books including fiction, non-fiction and poetry and these books encourage a love for reading. We curate these books and talk about them to entice children to read a wide range of books. In Nursery and Reception, children have access to the reading corner every day in their free flow time and the books are continually refreshed. Reception and KS1 children take home a ‘Reading for Pleasure’ book weekly whilst KS2 take home a book of their choosing which is changed as it finished. Children log these in their class ‘Reading for Pleasure’ record books.
Children across the school have regular opportunities to engage with a wide range of Reading for Pleasure events (book fairs, author visits, workshops and events such as World Book Day).
Assessment is used to monitor progress and to identify any child needing additional support as soon as they need it.
Statutory assessment
Ongoing formative assessment is conducted throughout lessons and is further informed by their Big Picture lessons. Teacher judgements are uploaded to Sonar half termly. This is then used to inform planning and support discussions at pupil progress meetings where allocation of further support or intervention is identified; this ensures that all children continue to make good progress from their starting points.

Geography
At our school, we aim to develop pupils’ understanding of the world, its environments, and the people who live within it. Our geography curriculum is structured using the Haringey Education Partnership Opening Worlds programme, providing a coherent, knowledge-rich framework that supports progression across Key Stage 2.
The Opening Worlds curriculum enables pupils to build a secure body of substantive knowledge about both physical and human geography. Pupils explore a range of places, environments, and geographical processes, developing an understanding of how the world is shaped and how people interact with it. Learning is carefully sequenced to ensure that knowledge is built cumulatively and revisited over time.
A strong emphasis is placed on developing geographical vocabulary, which is explicitly taught and reinforced to support pupils in describing and explaining geographical concepts with accuracy. Through this, pupils are able to make connections between different locations and themes, deepening their overall understanding of the subject.
Disciplinary knowledge is central to our geography teaching. Pupils are encouraged to think like geographers by asking questions, interpreting a range of sources such as maps, photographs, and data, and drawing informed conclusions. They develop an understanding of key concepts including place, space, scale, and interdependence, enabling them to analyse the relationships between people and their environments.
Fieldwork and enquiry-based learning provide opportunities for pupils to apply their knowledge in real-world contexts. These experiences help to develop observation, data collection, and analytical skills, while fostering a deeper connection to the local and wider environment.
By nurturing curiosity about the world and an understanding of global issues, we aim to equip pupils with the knowledge and skills they need to become informed, responsible citizens.

History
At our school, we aim to develop pupils’ understanding of the past and how it has shaped the world we live in today. Our history curriculum is structured using the Haringey Education Partnership Opening Worlds programme, which provides a carefully sequenced and knowledge-rich approach to learning.
The Opening Worlds curriculum is designed to build pupils’ understanding of significant historical periods, events, and individuals through a coherent and chronological framework. Pupils develop a secure body of substantive knowledge, while also learning how historians study the past. This includes understanding sources, interpreting evidence, and recognising how historical narratives are constructed.
Lessons are carefully structured to support long-term learning, with key knowledge revisited and built upon over time. Pupils are introduced to ambitious historical vocabulary, which is explicitly taught and regularly reinforced to support clear and accurate communication. Through this approach, children are able to make meaningful connections across different periods and civilisations.
Our curriculum places strong emphasis on developing disciplinary knowledge. Pupils are encouraged to ask questions, analyse sources, and consider different perspectives. They learn to understand concepts such as cause and consequence, continuity and change, and similarity and difference, enabling them to think critically about the past.
By fostering curiosity about the past and a deeper understanding of historical events and societies, we aim to equip pupils with the knowledge and skills they need to become thoughtful, informed citizens.

Maths
At our school, we are committed to developing confident, resilient mathematicians who can apply their knowledge and skills across a range of contexts. Our mathematics curriculum is carefully structured using the White Rose Maths scheme, ensuring clear progression, coherence, and depth of understanding for all pupils.
White Rose Maths supports a mastery approach, where children are encouraged to explore concepts in depth before moving on. Lessons are designed to build small, connected steps in learning, enabling pupils to develop a secure and flexible understanding of mathematical concepts. We place a strong emphasis on the use of mathematical language, reasoning, and problem-solving, ensuring that pupils can explain their thinking clearly and justify their answers.
Our teaching is also informed by evidence from the Education Endowment Foundation (EEF). This includes the use of high-quality questioning, explicit instruction, and carefully sequenced learning to reduce cognitive load. We recognise the importance of prior knowledge and ensure that key concepts are revisited regularly to strengthen retention through Flashback Four at the start of every lesson. Misconceptions are identified and addressed promptly, allowing all pupils to make sustained progress.
Concrete, pictorial, and abstract representations are used throughout the curriculum to support understanding. Pupils first explore concepts using practical resources, then move to visual representations, and finally to more abstract methods. This approach ensures that all learners, including those with additional needs, can access and succeed in mathematics.
We are dedicated to ensuring that all pupils experience success in mathematics. Through adaptive teaching, timely interventions, and targeted support, we aim to close gaps and provide appropriate challenge for every child. Opportunities for reasoning and problem-solving are embedded in every lesson, encouraging pupils to think deeply and apply their learning in a variety of contexts.
By fostering a positive attitude towards mathematics and promoting perseverance, we aim to equip our pupils with the skills and confidence they need to succeed both in school and beyond.
